Confirmed bug

Field Detail
Title Google Street View/map point can be opened from Room but not from Tour in VR
Severity Major - a Tour user cannot access the map-point navigation flow that is available from Room.
Reproduction 1. Launch the current Quest build. 2. From Room, open Google Street View/map and select a point: location opens successfully. 3. Open a Tour. 4. Attempt to open the same Google Street View/map point flow. 5. The map-point flow is unavailable/not usable.
Expected From a Tour, the user can open the map, pan/zoom, and select a point to load the corresponding Street View location, consistently with the Room flow.
Actual Point selection works from Room but cannot be performed from Tour.
Code-review evidence Room.cs calls mapsPanoConnector.LoadPanoByLatlong(longitude, latitude) for its Street View figures. MapsControls.cs supports controller click through connector.OnMapClick(lng, lat, null). In contrast, PanoramaController.cs only enables the Tour map button when activeTour["detail"]["widgets"]["map"]["widget"] == "SchemeKavftigComponent"; otherwise it hides MainUI.instance.mapsBtn. This conditional is the primary code path to investigate for the Tour-only regression.
Suggested fix direction Ensure the Tour's Google Street View/map widget is enabled and routes controller point selection to the same OnlineMapsPanoConnector flow used successfully in Room. Validate all supported map-widget types rather than hiding the map UI for non-SchemeKavftigComponent values.

QA Test Summary - historical 2024 task, reviewed 2026-07-29

Verdict: PASS - appropriate setup for the 2024 Oculus/Meta XR implementation

Issue #13 was created in the 2024 project context. The relevant baseline is Unity 2022.3.44f1 (the 2024-09-20 project revision), Meta XR SDK 68.0.1, and Oculus XR Plugin 4.2.0. In that implementation, controller input is intentionally handled through Meta's OVRInput APIs rather than Unity's separate Input System package. The empty InputActions.asset and RuntimeActionBindings.json were placeholders introduced in the 2024 initialization history and are not consumed by the production VR input path. They are therefore not a coding bug for this historical task.
